column1: # Canonical failure taxonomy shared by native BiSheng and the lightweight model.
# BiSheng and the model report pre-PlanMemory failures in different vocabularies:
# BiSheng emits MLIR diagnostics ("loc(...): error: 'op' op message"), the model
# throws "stage[function]: operation: reason".  Comparing them at the highest
# tier -- same failure reason class, not merely "both failed" -- requires
# mapping both vocabularies onto one canonical class id.
# Columns:
#   class_id     canonical failure class; the unit that must match
#   side         bisheng | model | both   (which producer the pattern applies to)
#   severity     fatal | info | cascade
#                Only `fatal` classes participate in the comparison.
#                `info`    a pass notice that is not itself a failure and that
#                          only one side ever emits; comparing it would make
#                          every affected case report a spurious sequence
#                          difference.
#                `cascade` a downstream consequence of an earlier fatal failure
#                          (typically corruption after a failed rollback, which
#                          then trips an assertion).  It is not an independent
#                          reason, and a model that lacks the underlying
#                          compiler bug cannot reproduce it, so requiring it to
#                          match would be an unreachable bar.
#                Both are still shown in the reported raw diagnostics.
#   pattern      Python regex matched against a NORMALIZED diagnostic line
#                (see normalize_diagnostic_line in validation_common.py:
#                loc() prefixes, temp paths, addresses and numbers are already
#                stripped before matching)
#   description  human note; not used by the comparator
# A diagnostic line matching no pattern is classified as "unclassified:<line>",
# which never compares equal to anything else.  That is deliberate: an unknown
# failure must show up as a mismatch and force a taxonomy update, rather than
# being silently bucketed with a known class.
class_id
